name: OpenCloud
tagline: A lean file-sharing server with no database to run
description: A file sync and sharing platform written in Go, forked in 2025 from ownCloud Infinite Scale. It keeps files and their metadata on disk rather than in a database, and offers a web interface, desktop and mobile sync clients, shared spaces for teams and browser editing through a connected office suite.
backing: OpenCloud GmbH (Germany), part of the Heinlein Group, funded by support and enterprise subscriptions

maturity.rationale: A young project on an older foundation: the code it forked had years of development behind it, but OpenCloud itself, its releases and its clients date from 2025. Promising, with a short track record.

selfHosting.summary: A single service started with Docker Compose, with no database to install or tune. A production setup still needs TLS, a proper sign-in provider once there are more than a few users, and backups of the data directory; office editing means running Collabora or ONLYOFFICE alongside.

requirements.notes: Storage is whatever your files need.

strengths: No database: files live on disk, where ordinary backup tools can reach them
Fast and light compared with PHP-based file platforms
Spaces give teams shared folders that do not belong to any one person
Single sign-on over OpenID Connect is built in
weaknesses: Young: a short track record as a project, and few independent hosting providers
It does files, not calendars, contacts or chat, and has far fewer add-ons than Nextcloud
Browser editing needs a separate office server
